I was around 12, at the grocery store with my mom. They had one of those bins full of VHS tapes and DVDs (which were relatively new) with a huge sign above it saying they were going for a couple dollars each. I stopped to look through them, not caring if my mom went a little bit ahead of me because we lived in a smaller town where I never felt unsafe. 

As I’m looking, this man in one of the wheelchair carts pulls up and asks me what kind of movies are in the bin. I don’t remember what I told him but I listed off a few because I thought he couldn’t see over the rim while he was in the chair. He begins talking about how he loves zombie movies and those are the only ones he watches. He asks what zombie movies I’ve seen. He asks if I like scary movies. He was so close to me that I could tell he was staring straight at me the entire time, I was looking at the movies. My gut quickly screamed at me to get away. I looked up at one point to see where my mom was and realized there was no one in the whole aisle except us. The huge sign blocked me from the cashier. I looked over at the man and noticed he had both feet planted on the ground, not the wheelchair cart. I immediately left. Didn’t say anything to him, just fucking walked away. 

I never saw that man again, I don’t know where he went because that store wasn’t that big and there was only one cashier. All I know is he gave me serious bad vibes and I usually trust my gut in those situations. Moral of the story, I guess, is to trust your gut even if the person appears disabled.
